Kevin Trudeau says rich and broke people spend money in opposite directions.

A broke person buys a boat. The moment it's in the water, it starts losing value - and it costs money just to keep running.

A rich person buys fine art, or stocks that pay dividends. Both go up in value. Neither costs anything to own.

The rich person still gets the boat eventually - but only after the dividends and interest are already paying for it. Rich people simply think differently than broke people.

Look at your last big purchase. Did it make you money, or just cost you money?

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #moneymindset #financialfreedom #richmindset #investing

Kevin Trudeau's parents were never in debt. His mom had one rule: if you can't pay cash for it, you can't afford it.

She'd watch the neighbors get a new car or new siding, then whisper that they were drowning in debt. Buying on credit just means paying interest on top of the price.

The fix Kevin Trudeau teaches: take 10% of every paycheck before you spend a dime, and put it in a separate account.

Can't afford to save 10%? Then you're spending money you don't have - sell something, cut something, but find it.

You pay yourself first. That comes straight out of The Richest Man in Babylon.

#kevintrudeau #financialfreedom #moneymindset #richestmaninbabylon #budgeting #wealthmindset

Kevin Trudeau's advice to a couple drowning in bills: you have equity in that house. Sell it.

They loved the house - or thought they did. Turns out they'd only lived there six years. Not exactly a lifetime of memories.

So they sold it, had a garage sale, and invested every dollar instead of spending it.

Three years later they told Kevin Trudeau: "We're already earning $10,000 a year on our investments, and we don't have to do anything." They've since lost weight, saved more, and started having more fun than they've had in years.

What's sitting in your house that could be working for you instead?

#kevintrudeau #realestate #wealthmindset #financialfreedom #moneymindset #investing

Blaine Athorn tried out for his high school football team. He didn't make it.

Kevin Trudeau says Blaine was embarrassed - he knew he simply wasn't in shape. So he decided something: next year, he was making that team.

He ran hills. He trained with extra weight strapped on. He didn't stop until the next season's tryouts.

When tryouts came, he was faster than everyone and stronger than everyone. He didn't just make the team - he became a starter. Sometimes losing is exactly what motivates you to come back stronger.

What tryout did you fail that you still haven't gone back for?

#kevintrudeau #successmindset #mindsetshift #discipline #motivation #hardwork

Kevin Trudeau was in a hot tub on a billionaire's yacht in Sydney Harbor when his cell phone rang.

It was Robert Kiyosaki, author of Rich Dad Poor Dad, asking if Kevin knew an investor named Renee Rifkin. Kevin was sitting right next to him - it was Rifkin's yacht, his own 50/50 partner in a venture that did $300 million in two years.

Kiyosaki's real lesson, Kevin says, is simple: stop buying things that lose value. Buy things that go up in value and cost you nothing to hold - that's how you become financially independent.

Which one did your last purchase do?
